outcomes.original: Filing step: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State and obtain an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS online. What to say: File Articles of Organization (LLC, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (corporation, $100) on the Secretary of State's bizfile portal, then apply for an EIN at irs.gov the same day (free, issued immediately Mon–Fri). The entity name and EIN are needed for every subsequent filing, the bank account, the lease, and the ABC application. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 LLC, $25 corporation).

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN) and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk. What to say: Apply for a Business Registration Certificate on the Treasurer's portal using the EIN and entity name; the BAN is issued within 1–5 days and is required by every city department. File the FBN statement at the County Clerk (in person or by mail, $60–$120) if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, then publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC require the filed FBN statement.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, including environmental review (likely a categorical exemption), a project description, a business plan, and renderings or floor plans. What to say: Submit the CUA application on the Planning portal with the BAN, the lease or proof of site control, a narrative explaining the concept as a bona fide eating place serving beer and wine, a menu, proposed hours (e.g. 7 AM–11 PM), a commitment to comply with Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD lighting, glazing and signage requirements, and a good-neighbor plan (sidewalk maintenance, soundproofing, odor control, waste management, community liaison). Planning will route the application for environmental review (typically a categorical exemption under CEQA for infill restaurant use), schedule a hearing 90–180 days out, and mail 300-foot notice. Comparable restaurant CUAs on this corridor took 2–13 months from filing to approval; the fee is adjusted annually by CPI and was about $3,150 for a no-construction CUA in 2026–27 per the catalog.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA and hire a food safety manager to complete a certified exam (ServSafe or equivalent) before filing the health permit application. What to say: Register for a seller's permit on the CDTFA online services portal using the EIN (free, often issued same day); ABC will not issue an alcohol licence until the seller's permit is on file. At least one owner or employee must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe, Prometric, 360training, $100–$250) within 60 days of opening; DPH asks for the certificate number on the health permit application and inspectors verify it at the pre-opening inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit DPH plan check for the kitchen layout, finishes, equipment and menu at the same time as or immediately after filing the building permit application. What to say: Upload two sets of scaled drawings (floor plan, equipment schedule, finishes schedule, plumbing isometric, mechanical ventilation), interior and exterior photos, the menu, and the food safety manager certificate to the DPH Environmental Health portal with the BAN, Location ID (LIN from Business Registration) and EIN. Select the 'new restaurant' plan check tier ($2,207 flat fee for 8 hours as of FY2026–27, billed at $276/hr for extra review). DPH will review within 21–60 days and either approve the plans or request corrections; after approval, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% construction complete and a final inspection at least two weeks before the target opening date. Do not open to the public until DPH issues the permit.
outcomes.note: Records confirm plan check requirement, fees, timeline and inspection scheduling but do not specify the detailed submittal requirements, timing relative to building permit, or list of required drawings.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements (kitchen build-out, hood, restrooms, ADA upgrades, any change of occupancy) with plans stamped by a licensed architect and routed to Planning, DPH, SFFD and SFPUC. What to say: Submit the building permit on DBI's online portal with architectural plans showing the proposed layout, equipment, exits, occupant load, accessibility compliance, and any structural, plumbing, mechanical or electrical work. The plans must be stamped by a California-licensed architect. DBI will route the application to Planning (for zoning conformance and CUA tracking), DPH (for food facility plan check), SFFD (if occupant load ≥50 or if a commercial hood is installed), and SFPUC (for FOG/grease interceptor review). Fees are a percentage of construction valuation (typically $800–$15,000); separate electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits are pulled by licensed subcontractors. The building permit is not issued until the CUA is granted and all plan-check corrections are completed.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the Health Permit to Operate after construction is substantially complete, DPH plan check is approved, and the certified food safety manager is on staff. What to say: Submit the Health Permit to Operate application on the DPH portal ($470 as of FY2026–27, includes initial inspection; annual licence fee is $0 for restaurants in 2026–28) with the BAN, LIN, EIN, and the food safety manager certificate number. Schedule the final inspection with your plan reviewer at least two weeks in advance; the inspector will verify that the facility matches the approved plans, all equipment is installed and operational, hand sinks and three-compartment sinks are in place, hot water is available, all surfaces are sealed and smooth, and food handler cards are posted. DPH issues the permit after the inspection passes; reinspections are billed at $276/hr. Do not serve the public until the permit is issued.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain workers' compensation insurance, register with EDD as an employer, subscribe to organics recycling, and secure ASCAP and BMI music licences before the first day of operation. What to say: Purchase workers' comp insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund (required from the first employee, premiums are 2–6% of payroll for restaurant class codes); several city permits ask for proof of coverage. Register as an employer with EDD within 15 days of paying wages over $100 (free, online, 1–7 days). Subscribe to commercial organics (green bin) collection with Recology or your hauler to comply with SB 1383 before the health inspection. Sign up for ASCAP and BMI blanket licences ($300–$2,500/year each, formula-based on occupancy and music use) at ascap.com and bmi.com; the licences are effective immediately and federal copyright law requires them to play recorded music publicly.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $6,293 to $20,850. Notes: The timeline of 120–300 days and government cost of $6,300–$20,900 cover the three approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval per the comparable cases, estimated $3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost and fee waiver eligibility per the catalog), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days from application to issuance after plan check and final inspection, $470 application + $828–$2,500 plan check as of FY2026–27), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days for plan review and issuance, $800–$15,000 based on construction valuation). The day range is time to approval when those approvals are granted; it does not include time to a denial or withdrawal, and it assumes the Calle 24 frontage cap does not prohibit the use. The ABC Type 41 licence is not included in the path because its status is insufficient information (the transaction type is unknown and undue-concentration rules cannot be applied), but if it were a new licence or transfer from outside the census tract, add 60–180 days and $1,000–$1,600 ABC fees plus potential PCN hearing time. Also budget for entity formation and business registration ($125–$270, 1–10 days), seller's permit and EDD (free), food safety manager cert ($100–$250), RBS training for alcohol servers ($3–$30 per person), FBN filing and publication ($60–$120, 35 days), workers' comp insurance (2–6% of annual payroll), FOG interceptor installation (included in building permit construction cost), sign permit if exterior signage changes ($300–$1,500, 7–45 days), and ASCAP/BMI music licences ($600–$5,000/year combined). The cost figures are government fees only and exclude construction, architect and consultant fees, insurance premiums (except the zero-fee workers' comp registration), and rent during the approval period.
